post.title: The Miracle Doesn't Meet You Where You Wait | Luke 17
post.description:
There are miracles that are received only when men are in motion.

The miracle is somewhere in your journey, but you won't see it until you have moved.

Move!

slides.title:
The Miracle
Doesn't Meet You
Where You *Wait*.
slides.sub: Ten lepers, a wedding in Cana, and a river that would not part — three miracles that all waited for the same thing before they showed up.

slides.lead: In Luke 17, 10 lepers came to Jesus, seeking to be cleansed.
slides.body: Jesus spoke to them from a distance and asked them to go show themselves to the priest.

slides.lead: Showing themselves to the priest is what they should do after they have been cleansed.
slides.body: Yet, Jesus asked them to do so while they were *yet lepers*.

slides.lead: The bible says while they were on their way, they were cleansed.
slides.body: They didn't receive the miracle until they *WERE ON THEIR WAY*.

slides.lead: At Cana Jesus instructed the men to take "water" to the chief of the ceremony at a time when wine was needed.
slides.body: The water didn't become wine *until they moved*.

slides.lead: The priests (when Israel wanted to cross the Jordan) didn't see the river path until they stepped their feet in the water.
slides.body: There are miracles that are received only when men are *in motion*.

slides.lead: While you are waiting for miracles to happen before you move, God has purposed that it is when you have moved that you'd see the miracles.
slides.body: There are miracles that can only be received by people who are *in motion*.

slides.quote: The miracle is somewhere in your journey, but you won't see it *until you have moved*.
